labels.label: T-abs-dec8-minimal-witness/1-causality
labels.notes: halfLightLine (Dec8MinimalWitness.lean:90-110) is exactly the sketch: le U x y := (x = y ∧ x ∈ U) ∨ (0 ≤ x ∧ x ≤ y ∧ Icc x y ⊆ U), lt := False. I read every field of Causal.Causality (Causal/Causality.lean:55-86). le_mem_left/right: x, y ∈ Icc x y ⊆ U. le_refl: the diagonal. le_trans: if either step is the diagonal it collapses, otherwise Icc x z ⊆ Icc x y ∪ Icc y z ⊆ U and 0 ≤ x carries over. le_mono (V ≤ U, le V x y ⇒ le U x y): the diagonal case uses h on x ∈ V, the segment case composes Icc x y ⊆ V ⊆ U. The direction is right and the field typechecks against the structure's binder order. lt_*, le_of_lt and isOpen_lt_*: vacuous or {y | False} = ∅ open. defi:categorie_C allows an empty ≪ (transitive, contained in ≤, open), as for the library's lightlikeLine and spacelikeLine. The structure is genuine and not vacuous: ≤ is non-trivial on [0, ∞). The docstring's 'spacelike line below 0, lightlike line from 0' matches Causal/Lines.lean:95, :113.

labels.label: T-abs-dec8-minimal-witness/2-arc-connected
labels.notes: CausallyArcConnected = CausallyArcConnectedOn ⊤ (Causal/ArcConnected.lean:127-133), both directions for ≤ and ≪ on every open U. The proof goes through causallyArcConnectedOn_iff (:156), which proves curve ⇒ relation in every spacetime, so only relation ⇒ curve is owed. It uses the constant curve for x = y, and for 0 ≤ x < y the affine curve, its CausalCurveOn obtained from timelikeLine_chronalCurveOn_affine with every intermediate point ≥ 0. The ≪ half is vacuous. halfLightLine_causallyArcConnectedOn W, for every W, comes from CausallyArcConnectedOn.mono. The REPORT's side remark that a causal curve from a negative point is constant is true (the set where c = c(0) is open and closed in [0, 1]) and is not used.

labels.label: T-abs-dec8-minimal-witness/3-absolutely-minimal
labels.notes: halfLightLine_absolutelyMinimal is the library's AbsolutelyMinimal (Causal/Generated.lean:247, the verbatim def:topological_space_causality_absolutely: every cover of M generates Q), via CausallyArcConnected.absolutelyMinimal (cor:causalement_connexe_minimal, ArcConnected.lean:216). halfLightLine_absolutelyMinimalOn W holds for EVERY open W (Generated.lean:239: for every S covering W, every V ≤ W, ≤_V and ≪_V are TransGen of the steps ≤_{V ⊓ O}, ≪_{V ⊓ O}, O ∈ S). On the gluing reading: OQ-18 phrases it as '≤ generated by covers, i.e. absolute minimality'. Read as the cosheaf condition that axiom (b) forces (the inclusions are the C-morphisms, and a colimit of preorders is the transitive closure of the union), it asks, for every open W and every open cover of W, that ≤_W and ≪_W be generated by the pieces. That is the V = W instance of AbsolutelyMinimalOn W. Conversely, the V ≤ W instance is the same condition at V for the cover {V ⊓ O}. So '∀ W, AbsolutelyMinimalOn W' is EXACTLY the gluing reading, for ≤ and ≪ alike (≪ is empty, so its half holds trivially in any reading). It also implies the library's AbsolutelyMinimal (absolutelyMinimal_iff, the W = ⊤ case). No gap.

labels.label: T-abs-dec8-minimal-witness/4-causally-open-future
labels.notes: CausallyOpenFuture (Causal/Properties.lean:121) quantifies over every open U and every open V ≤ U, the printed def:causally_open_spacetime_open (ETT.tex:694-697, quoted verbatim in the docstring). The proof (:173-192) takes arbitrary U and V. If y ∈ J⁺_U(V) is reached by the diagonal, or by x = y, then V ⊆ J⁺_U(V) (reflexivity) is a neighbourhood. If 0 ≤ x < y with [x, y] ⊆ U, it takes an interval (l, u) ∋ y inside U, and every z ∈ (max l x, u) has x ≤ z and [x, z] ⊆ [x, y] ∪ (l, u) ⊆ U. No assumption is made on V meeting one side of 0 or on U containing [0, ∞): a negative x contributes only its own point, which V covers. I checked by hand on U = (-1, 1) ∪ (2, 3), V = (-1/2, 1/2): J⁺ = (-1/2, 1), open. halfLightLine_locallyCausallyOpenFuture comes via CausallyOpenFuture.locallyCausallyOpenFuture (LadderLocal.lean:257).

labels.label: T-abs-dec8-minimal-witness/5-not-causally-open
labels.notes: halfLightLine_Jminus_Ioo: Jminus ⊤ (Ioo 1 2) = Ico 0 2 exactly. ⊆: y = x ∈ (1, 2), or 0 ≤ y ≤ x < 2. ⊇: for y ∈ [0, 2) the point (max y 1 + 2)/2 ∈ (1, 2) lies above y. I also checked that perturbing the right-hand side to Ico 0 3 makes the file fail to elaborate. It is not open: 0 is in it and l/2 < 0 is not. halfLightLine_not_causallyOpen negates DEC-8's CausallyOpen (Properties.lean:130, second conjunct with U = ⊤, V = (1, 2)). halfLightLine_not_causallyOpenPast is ¬ dual.CausallyOpenFuture, the same set through dual_Jplus.

labels.label: T-abs-dec8-minimal-witness/6-local
labels.notes: LocallyCausallyOpen = LCOF ∧ dual.LCOF (LadderLocal.lean:152), two-sided as DEC-8. _of_zero_mem: for W ∋ 0 with (l, u) ⊆ W, J⁻_W((0, u)) contains 0 (0 ≤_W u/2) and no negative point. _of_zero_notMem: if 0 ∉ W, a point y below x ≠ y has 0 < y, and the neighbourhood (max l 0, min u x) stays below x with its segment in U. Both proofs checked. So an open set is causally open in the past iff it misses 0: the localisation 'exactly at 0' is proved in both directions. The remark that the result also follows from AbsolutelyMinimal.causallyOpen_of_locallyCausallyOpen is true and is not used.

labels.label: T-abs-dec8-minimal-witness/7-ladder
labels.notes: Each claim was checked against its definition. PushUp (Properties.lean:69) via pushUp_iff, vacuous because ≪ = ∅, disclosed as vacuous. IsCausal: ≤ lies inside the real order. GloballyHyperbolic: diamond ⊤ p q = Icc p q for p ≥ 0, and ⊆ {p} for p < 0, so it is compact. StronglyCausalOpen: open intervals contain the diamonds of their points (diamond ⊆ Icc). HasTimeFunction (CurvesExtend.lean:516; the ladder node, a continuous T strictly increasing along ≤ ⊤): id, explicitly not the paper's IsTimeFunction. Not Tarentin: at −1 with neighbourhood Iio 0, the interior of a diamond from a negative vertex is ⊆ {p}, and a non-empty open interval is infinite. No ChronalNeighbours: lt is False. Not CausallyPlain: interior J⁺_⊤(univ) = univ while closure I⁺ = ∅.

labels.label: T-abs-dec8-minimal-witness/8-separation
labels.notes: halfLightLine_separates_causallyOpen conjoins the 13 positive and 5 negative properties listed in the REPORT. LocallyPushUp, CausallyCompact, StronglyCausal and CurvesExtend come from strict-library edges (PushUp.locallyPushUp, GloballyHyperbolic.causallyCompact, StronglyCausalOpen.stronglyCausal, HasTimeFunction.curvesExtend). The five bare forms say what their names say. Each is ¬ ∀ C : Causality ℝ, (hypotheses) → conclusion, and the extra hypotheses in the arc-connected form only strengthen the non-implication. The gluing form takes (∀ W, AbsolutelyMinimalOn W), the exact gluing reading (label 3). halfLightLine_dual_separates is correct: dual.dual = C by rfl, dual_absolutelyMinimal. 'Either reading' is NOT overstated: the witness is a library Causality (the no-gluing 'equivalently' form, kb/0014), satisfies the gluing condition on every open for every cover (label 3), and lives on ℝ (Hausdorff, second countable). So causally_open_future ⇏ causally_open holds among absolutely minimal ETT spacetimes in both readings OQ-18 names, and OQ-67 (b) does not bear on this pair. Findings 1 and 3 are true. Finding 2's mathematical content is true; its wording is the minor finding below. Scope beyond the REPORT, recorded for OQ-67, not a defect: the witness has ≪ = ∅ (no chronal neighbours, not plain). So it is also silent on whether the ± matters among causally plain or chronological absolutely minimal spacetimes (Minkowski, E_α), not only among tarentin ones. The ladder already gives push_up ∧ chronal_neighbours ⇒ causally_open, so a witness with chronal neighbours would have to fail push-up. The keeper's simulated counts (22 / 14) were not re-run; the [[open]] note the REPORT cites (programme/ladder.toml:1426-1429 at HEAD) is as quoted.

findings.what: The mathematical content is proved: not_dual_causallyOpenFuture_of_absolutelyMinimal_bare, so the J⁺-only notion is not time-symmetric among absolutely minimal causalities. The attribution to the paper overreaches in two ways. (i) It says 'the paper's past-from-future arguments (e.g. …)', but the proof of prop:tarentin_topological_spacetime_causality (ii)⇒(i), at ETT.tex:745-746 (J⁻(J̊⁻(b_i)) = J̊⁻(b_i)), is the only proof in ETT.tex that invokes causal openness for J⁻. (ii) 'Silently assume it does not' presents as a fresh defect what OQ-9 already raised and DEC-8 settled: under DEC-8's J± that step is covered, and the proposition is 'closed as stated'. The finding bears only on the branch of OQ-67 (a) that keeps the printed form.
